clue.text: Solar smoke ?

definitions.meaning: stands for the sun's outer glowing atmosphere, the halo seen in an eclipse
a smoke is a cigar, and this is a brand-like name for a long straight-sided cigar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solar' is an adjective standing in for the sun's halo, a loose fit the question mark excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun's luminous halo and a long cigar share this one name.

clue.text: Patients with high temperatures discharged in wartime once

parts.note: a doctor's cases are patients
feverish, so hot

explanation.surface: Fever patients sent home from a wartime hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' suggests patients leaving hospital; it means fired from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Old artillery ammunition of small balls in a canister, fired in past wars.

clue.text: In the right hand, bird is needing no bush?

indicators.note: the bird and is sit within the right hand

parts.note: a hen is a bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'good wine needs no bush' (no tavern sign) makes the definition: wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhine wine, good wine needing no bush, the ivy that once advertised a tavern.

clue.text: Food in term is cooked and eaten by teachers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the teachers' union, eaten by it

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers

indicators.note: cooking reworks the letters of in term

explanation.surface: Meals during school term are prepared and consumed by staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooked' rearranges the clue's own 'in term'; the teachers are the UK National Union of Teachers, and 'Food' at the front is the definition, not the meal being cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment, anything that feeds.

clue.text: Dropped from the twelfth party? That's a side-issue

parts.note: to be dropped from a list is to be off it
the Glorious Twelfth (12 August) opens the grouse season, so its party is a shoot

explanation.surface: Someone left out of a grouse-shooting party is told the matter is a sideshow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, is the start of grouse shooting in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or branch growing from a main stem is a side-issue.

clue.text: General direction in shooting " The Papal Seal "

indicators.note: the general and direction go inside the shooting word

parts.note: firing is shooting
Sherman was a US Civil War general
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A general orders shooting at the Pope's seal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's signet ring, showing St Peter casting a net.

clue.text: How to speed the parting cat — The Bard

definitions.text: How to speed the parting cat
definitions.meaning: throw hot water at it, a play on 'speed the parting guest'
a Norse court poet, also spelt with K

explanation.walkthrough: Pope's 'welcome the coming, speed the parting guest' is twisted: burn the cat to send it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn with hot liquid would send a cat fleeing; the same word is a variant for an old Norse poet.

clue.text: One able to fly or to land with tail shot off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of land is removed

explanation.surface: A bird may take flight or come down to earth, its tail shot away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail shot off' drops the D from LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunting, a bird, so one able to fly.

clue.text: Power of the County

definitions.meaning: the actor ... Power, so the first name of Power

explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone Power was a Hollywood star; 'Power' looks like strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The film star's first name is also an Ulster county.

clue.text: In contract the sole winner, we hear

definitions.text: In contract the sole winner, we hear

parts.words: In contract the sole winner, we hear
parts.note: the devil in Faust wins a soul by a pact; sole said aloud is soul

explanation.walkthrough: In the Faust legend, the devil's agent signs a contract to gain Faust's soul; 'sole' is a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil of the Faust story, who wins Faust's soul by a pact.

clue.text: Enigmatic product of the strong

parts.note: Samson's riddle in Judges: 'out of the strong came forth' honey from a lion's carcass; the riddle's product is what came forth

explanation.walkthrough: Samson's riddle reads 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth' this.
explanation.definitionFit: The riddle's answer is honey, whose quality is sugary taste, the thing that came out of the strong lion.

clue.text: Oil's essential for a sailor at the start

indicators.note: tells us the word at comes at the start, before the sailor

parts.note: a tar is old slang for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman is advised that oil matters from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil's essential' reads as 'oil is vital' but means an essential oil, distilled from rose petals.
explanation.definitionFit: This perfume is an essential oil pressed from rose petals.

clue.text: Visitors to Aeaea became at home in smart surroundings

indicators.note: the smart word wraps around the at-home word, giving surroundings to it

parts.note: swish means smart, stylish
in means at home

explanation.surface: Guests on a Greek island grew comfortable in elegant lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Aeaea is Circe's island in the Odyssey, where she turned Odysseus's crew into pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe's visitors were changed into pigs, so they became piggish.

clue.text: A long time to grasp the image is a phantom

indicators.note: the long time holds the image within it, grasping it

parts.note: an eon is an age, a very long time
an idol is a graven image

explanation.surface: Something that endures for ages yet is only a ghostly picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek word for a spectre or apparition.

clue.text: Colour of French rock perhaps

indicators.note: signals the French word may be jumbled into another form

parts.note: roche is French for rock

explanation.surface: A question about the shade of stone found in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ROCHE, French for rock, and rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy yellow-brown pigment and shade.

clue.text: A paper-back one for the interval

indicators.note: the paper's name is read backwards, paper-back

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paperback book chosen to read during the theatre break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper-back' looks like a book format; it means the paper's name turned back, giving SEMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-step in music is the smallest interval between notes.

clue.text: Thrashing needed by " Eureka " man to dry up

definitions.text: needed by " Eureka " man to dry up
definitions.meaning: Archimedes cried 'Eureka' in his bath, and would need cloth to dry himself

explanation.walkthrough: Archimedes leapt from his bath crying 'Eureka', so needed drying.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating, and the absorbent bath-cloth fabric.

clue.text: Wastes fruit that has taken a battering?

definitions.text: fruit that has taken a battering?
definitions.meaning: fried fruit pieces coated in batter

explanation.walkthrough: 'battering' suggests a beating; it means coating in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Squanders, and fried battered pieces of fruit.

clue.text: Cowardly fellow to cut off back to a Scottish resort

indicators.note: the word for cut off is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
Troon is a golfing resort on the Ayrshire coast

explanation.surface: A timid man flees back to the Scottish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: TROON is a seaside golf resort in Ayrshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an abject coward.

clue.text: Main Island and a lot of others

parts.note: the main is the sea, ocean

explanation.surface: Sea, an island and a heap of other islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific region of countless islands.

clue.text: Drink too much for Ophelia

definitions.meaning: drink as a noun, the sea or a glass of liquid
Laertes in Hamlet: 'Too much of ... hast thou, poor Ophelia', after she drowns

explanation.walkthrough: Ophelia drowns in a brook in Hamlet, and her brother says she has had too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is the plain liquid, and it was the liquid that drowned Ophelia.

clue.text: Sling mud at Italian leader, supporting a right revolution

indicators.note: in a down answer the leader sits under, supporting, the rest
a and right are turned round together

parts.note: Mussolini was Il Duce

explanation.surface: Insulting Mussolini while backing a right-wing uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns A RT into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame or slander someone.

clue.text: Birdman, looks up Chapter 101 in the Koran

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read backwards

parts.note: a sura is a chapter of the Koran
CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An ornithologist consults a chapter of the Koran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks up' turns SURA plus CI upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical boy who flew on wax wings, a birdman.

clue.text: Catty type, dishonest too, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for a dishonest person is spoken aloud

parts.note: a cheater is a dishonest one, and 'too' says this one is dishonest as well

explanation.surface: A spiteful person who is also a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without the final R sound, the word for a dishonest person sounds like the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spotted cat, so a type of cat.

clue.text: Cloth for the start of Buchan's cold spell?

definitions.text: Cloth for the start of Buchan's cold spell?

parts.words: Cloth for the start of Buchan's cold spell?
parts.note: a warm fabric for a cold snap; John Buchan's title, Lord ..., starts with this word

explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Buchan named recurring cold spells, and the novelist John Buchan became Lord Tweedsmuir.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen fabric from the Scottish Borders, worn against cold.

clue.text: Lamb-like at heart, entirely trusting

indicators.note: the Lamb-like word sits at the heart of the abbreviation

parts.note: right means entirely (right through), abbreviated RT
Charles Lamb wrote as Elia, so Elian means in the manner of Lamb

explanation.surface: Someone meek as a lamb deep down and wholly trustful.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb's essays were signed Elia; 'Lamb' looks like the animal but names the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who depends on another is trusting in them.

clue.text: To the Sun God is born the Queen of the East

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
née means born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A royal lady of the East is born to the Egyptian sun deity.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian queen, wife of a rajah.

clue.text: Its degrees may be taken from Greenwich

definitions.text: Its degrees may be taken from Greenwich

parts.words: Its degrees may be taken from Greenwich
parts.note: east-west map degrees are measured from the meridian at Greenwich; read as a university awarding degrees

explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich, in London, is where the prime meridian runs; 'degrees' suggests university qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular distance east or west is measured from the meridian at Greenwich.

clue.text: Longfellow hero would seem aloof, holding off

indicators.note: the hero's name holding the word off would give the aloof word, so off is taken out of it

parts.note: standoffish means aloof, distant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem's tall hero would look distant if he held back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the hero's name with OFF inside spells the word for aloof, so remove OFF from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Standish is the title hero of Longfellow's poem 'The Courtship of Miles Standish'.

clue.text: She's a man-eater so back to the ship!

indicators.note: the words for so and the ship are read backwards together

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A predatory woman appears, so everyone hurries back aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: ERGO plus SS read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A female giant who eats people in fairy tales.
